title: Mali Marks 66th Independence Day Amid Worsening Security Crisis
detail: Mali marked its Independence Day on September 22, 2026 — 66 years since independence from France in 1960 — with junta leader Assimi Goïta presiding over a military parade in Bamako while JNIM's fuel blockade and the fallout from the September 10 Dioura attack continued to strain the state. Al Jazeera reported that on September 14, more than 900 fuel tankers entered Bamako under military escort, underscoring how the capital now depends on armed convoys rather than open roads for its fuel supply. Control Risks senior analyst Beverly Ochieng said the JNIM-FLA alliance in the north "poses a threat to the government's consolidation of national territory." The UNHCR estimated more than 400,000 people internally displaced as of June 2026, and Mali's ICC withdrawal — begun in June — remains in process alongside its January 2025 ECOWAS exit.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — "Mali marks independence amid a worsening security crisis"

media.caption: Mali's Independence Day parade in Bamako amid the ongoing JNIM blockade and insurgency
